transcript.content: Hi, welcome in — I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Um, well... I guess my eating has just been really off lately. Some weeks I just... I don't really have an appetite for dinner at all. And then other times, I just find myself in the kitchen late at night, eating crackers and sweets when everyone else is asleep. It just felt like maybe I should come in.
Over the past few weeks, have you been feeling down, sad, or losing interest in things you normally enjoy?

Um... I suppose. I do go through these stretches sometimes where... I don't know, the house just feels sort of gray. And heavy. I'll just sit at the kitchen table for a while, feeling kind of... empty, I guess. Even if nothing terrible has actually happened that day. So... yeah.
When you eat those crackers and sweets late at night, do you find that you've actually woken up from sleep to eat, or are you still awake and just haven't gone to bed yet?

Um... no, I'm usually just still awake. I just... I can't really get to sleep, so I end up in the kitchen. Like I said before, my eating is just all over the place right now. That's really the main reason I decided to make the appointment. It's just... some weeks I barely touch dinner, and then other nights I'm just standing there in the dark eating sweets.
Does this pattern of skipping dinner or eating at night happen mainly during those times when you're feeling low and empty, or does it also happen on days when your mood feels pretty normal?

Um... I'm not really sure. I haven't really kept track of it like that. Like I said, that's just what finally pushed me to make the appointment... my eating just being so all over the place. I don't really know if it's connected to feeling empty or not. It just happens.
How long do these stretches of feeling low, empty, and heavy usually last—days, or do they go on for two weeks or more at a time?

Um... I don't know exactly how many days or weeks at a time. I haven't really counted. But... I guess if you add up all those gray periods... the times I feel guilty and just lose interest in things... it's probably been about seven months total. Something like that.
Over these past seven months, would you say the low, empty feeling has been present more days than not, or does it come and go with periods where your mood feels completely normal in between?

Um... I guess it comes in stretches. I don't really know if it's more days than not... but I just go through these stretches where the house just feels gray and... heavy. I'll just sit at the kitchen table, feeling empty. Even when nothing terrible has happened that day. It just... gets like that.
Thinking about the longest single stretch of feeling low and empty, about how many days in a row did that last before your mood lifted at all?
I... I really couldn't give you a number. It's hard to tell exactly when it starts and stops. The days just sort of blend together when it gets like that... so, I just don't know.

During those nighttime episodes when you're eating crackers and sweets, do you feel like you can't stop or control how much you're eating once you start, or do you feel like you're just choosing to snack because you're awake?

I don't know if it's about control... it's just... my eating is all over the place. Some weeks I barely touch dinner at all. And then other nights, I'm just standing there in the dark, eating crackers and whatever sweets I can find after everyone else is asleep. That's... that's actually what finally pushed me to come in, I guess. The eating being so unpredictable.
When you find yourself eating those crackers and sweets at night, do you feel upset, guilty, or ashamed about it afterward, or does it not really bother you emotionally?

I... yeah, I feel bad about it. But I feel bad about a lot of things. I can spend hours just... replaying small things. Like, I bought this expensive tube of pigment for my painting, and I just kept thinking about it. Or if I snap at my husband... I just feel like I've ruined the whole household. It just... sits with me.

Things I used to look forward to... they just feel like chores I keep putting off. Like my book club, or cooking... even going to galleries or tending the rose beds. I just... don't really care to do them.
During these past seven months, has there been any stretch of two months or longer where you felt completely back to your normal self, with no low or empty feelings at all?
No... I don't think so. Those... gray, guilty periods where I just lose interest in things... they've pretty much added up to about seven months now. I haven't really had a break.
During these past several months, have you also noticed a persistent lack of energy or feeling unusually tired, even without much physical exertion?
I... I don't really know. I guess I'm just... tired a lot. But I haven't really been paying attention to exactly how much.
During these low, empty periods, have you had any thoughts of death or of hurting yourself?

I... um. I don't know if I'd say I want to hurt myself. I haven't... planned anything like that. But sometimes... on the really bad nights... I just think it might be easier if I... if I just didn't wake up.
During those nighttime episodes, would you say you're eating a noticeably larger amount of food than most people would eat in that situation, or is it more just a few crackers or a sweet or two?

I... I guess it's a lot. It's not just a few crackers. It's... all over the place. Sometimes I barely touch dinner at all, and then... yeah, I just stand in the kitchen eating whatever I can find after everyone's asleep. It's... it's actually part of why I finally decided to come in.
Over the past few months, about how often would you say these nighttime binge-eating episodes happen—would you say it's at least once a week, or less often than that?

I... I don't know exactly how often. It's just... like I said, my eating has been all over the place. Some weeks I barely eat dinner, and then... other nights I'm just standing there eating crackers and sweets after everyone's gone to bed. That's... that's what finally pushed me to come in.
Have these low, empty feelings and low energy made it hard for you to keep up with your usual daily responsibilities, like household tasks or work, over these past several months?

I... I guess so. I've fallen behind on some things. I was doing this... facilitator training, and some work on a private blog. But my projects... and trying to explain things... it just got really hard to organize it all. And... well, there's been some tension at home, too. So keeping up our normal routines with my husband has been... difficult.

{"intent": "Determine severity of functional impairment (moderate vs. severe depressive episode) by clarifying whether she can still manage most daily responsibilities despite difficulty, or has become largely unable to carry

I mean... I'm still doing some things. It's just... like I said, I fell behind on the training and the blog. It just... got too hard to organize my thoughts for the projects. And... the tension with my husband, it just makes the normal routines... harder. But I'm still... I'm still doing what I have to.
Would you say that on most days you're now unable to carry out your usual responsibilities at all, or are you still managing to get through them even though it's difficult?

I'm... still getting through most of it, I guess. It's just... I'm behind on the facilitator training. And the private blog work. It's... organizing the projects and trying to explain things, it's just gotten really hard to manage. And the tension at home... it just makes keeping up the normal routines with my husband a lot harder. But I'm not... I'm not completely unable to do things.
Over just the past three months, can you estimate roughly how many nights per week you've had one of these large eating episodes—even a rough average, like two nights a week or five nights a week?

I don't know... it's just all over the place. Some weeks I barely eat dinner at all. And then... other nights, I'm just standing in the kitchen eating crackers and sweets after everyone else is asleep. That's... that's kind of what finally pushed me to come in.
Would you say those thoughts about not waking up happen only occasionally on your worst nights, or are they present almost every day now?
Just... occasionally. On the worst nights. I just think... maybe it would be easier if I didn't wake up. But... I haven't made a plan to hurt myself or anything.
